title: Enforce readiness gate before adding nodes to serving pools
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Internal: nodes will no longer be eligible for serving pools until Fleet Readiness reports Ready (behind feature flag). Includes kill switch + safe fallback behavior.
description:
## Summary
This PR enforces a readiness gate in the control plane so newly provisioned GPU nodes cannot be added to serving pools (Dedicated or shared) until they have passed provision-to-ready validations and are in `Ready` state. This closes a gap we saw during early rollout where nodes could join the pool after kubelet join but before validations (GPU health / driver parity / NCCL smoke / perf canary) completed, causing avoidable brownouts and noisy remediation.

The gate is feature-flagged and supports a rollback toggle. It also includes safety checks to avoid deadlocking pool scale-ups if readiness signals are missing/late.

## Motivation / Context
- During the staged rollout we observed instances where the autoscaler/pool controller saw a node as schedulable and added it to a serving pool while it was still in `Validating`, leading to:
  - GPU driver drift errors surfacing as runtime failures
  - NCCL fabric issues showing up as elevated latency / timeouts
  - Increased quarantine after traffic had already been routed
- We already have canonical readiness states defined in ADR-017 and exposed by Fleet Readiness Service; this PR makes the pool membership controller respect that state.

## Behavior change
- Prior behavior: pool membership controller would accept nodes if they were:
  - registered in cluster AND
  - labeled as a GPU worker AND
  - passed basic kubelet/node conditions (Ready/Schedulable)
- New behavior (when flag enabled): to be eligible for pool membership, node must additionally have `fleet_readiness_state == Ready`.
  - Nodes in `Allocated/Provisioning/Validating` are blocked from joining.
  - Nodes in `Quarantined` are explicitly denied (and if already present, they are removed/drained depending on pool policy).

## Feature flag / rollback
- New flag: `fleet.readiness_gate.enabled` (default: OFF)
  - Scopes: region + pool type (Dedicated/shared) via existing rollout config
  - Kill switch behavior: when disabled, reverts to previous eligibility logic immediately (no schema rollback required)
- New config: `fleet.readiness_gate.fail_open` (default: true for staged rollout)
  - If Fleet Readiness Service is unavailable or returns an "unknown" response, controller will allow membership but emits a high-severity metric + structured log event.
  - Rationale: avoid deadlocking capacity bring-up during transient readiness-service incidents; we can flip to fail-closed after confidence increases.

## Safety checks / edge cases
- Race protection: readiness transitions are polled with monotonic event timestamps; we only treat `Ready` as authoritative if it is newer than the current membership reconciliation start.
- Stuck validating: nodes blocked >N minutes emit `pool_membership_blocked_total{reason="validating_timeout"}` and include readiness failure reason pointer when available.
- Manual override: on-call can set an allowlist annotation `fleet.redwood.dev/skip-readiness-gate=true` on a node for emergency capacity recovery (audited + metric). This is intentionally noisy and not intended for routine use.

## Observability
- Metrics:
  - `pool_membership_gate_checks_total{result, reason, pool_type, region}`
  - `pool_membership_blocked_total{reason, pool_type, region}`
  - `pool_membership_gate_readiness_lookup_latency_ms{pool_type, region}`
  - `pool_membership_gate_fail_open_total{pool_type, region}`
- Logs:
  - `fleet_pool_membership_gate` structured event with node_id (redacted to hash), pool_id, readiness_state, readiness_artifact_ref

## Testing
- Unit tests for eligibility logic (Ready vs Validating vs Quarantined)
- Integration-style tests using fake readiness service:
  - fail-open path
  - unknown node path
  - override annotation path
- Manual verification in staging:
  - scaled a Dedicated A100 pool from 0->5; nodes held out until validations passed; membership added within ~30s after Ready.

## Rollout plan (follow-up)
- Enable flag in us-east A100 Dedicated only (ENG-4829 checklist) with fail-open=true
- Monitor:
  - time-to-ready P95 and blocked counts
  - any increase in pool scale-up time
- If stable for 48h, flip fail-open=false and expand scope

## Links
- Linear: ENG-4822, ENG-4825, ENG-4829
- Support context: SUP-28433 (nodes stuck in validating; previously could still get traffic)
- Related PRs: pr-18421 (readiness states/API), pr-18429 (validation artifacts), pr-18452 (quarantine on repeat failures)

review_conversation: Ethan Park: The fail-open default makes sense for rollout, but we should ensure we page loudly if we’re failing open for >5m. Can you add a counter + alert hook? Also confirm we don’t tag metrics with node_id.

Jordan Lee (author): Added `pool_membership_gate_fail_open_total{pool_type,region}` and removed node_id from all tags (log retains a hash only). Alert wiring will be in observability-pack PR; added TODO with owner (Aisha) + linked ENG-4827.
Vanessa Ortiz: For stuck nodes, can we expose the readiness failure reason pointer so fleet can triage quickly? Even if we can’t show full logs, an artifact ref helps.

Jordan Lee (author): Included `readiness_artifact_ref` in the log event when present, and we emit `reason="validating_timeout"` with a short string `failure_code` (low-cardinality) from readiness service.

Sean Gallagher: Concern about deadlock: if readiness service is degraded and we flip fail-closed too early, pools may not scale during incidents. Can we make the fail-open/closed policy per region so SRE can keep one region permissive temporarily?
Jordan Lee (author): Yes — `fleet.readiness_gate.fail_open` is now rollout-scoped by region via existing config. Also added an explicit runbook note in code comments for toggling during incidents.
Benji Okafor: Minor: readiness timestamp comparison looks off-by-one. If Ready event arrives exactly at reconciliation start, should we accept it? I think yes.
Jordan Lee (author): Good catch. Updated comparison to accept `>=` and added a test case for boundary condition.
Aisha Bello: Metrics look good. Please ensure `pool_id` isn’t a label (cardinality). Use pool_type + region only.
Jordan Lee (author): Removed `pool_id` from metric tags; kept it only in structured logs (with sampling).
Ethan Park: Approved after last push. Please coordinate enabling flag with release train checklist.
